tagline: Through the King George woods, along the edge of Caledon.
intro: Caledon Road leaves Passapatanzy and curves through the King George woods by way of Mustoe, Goby and Osso, with lanes turning north to the Potomac beach communities, Belvedere Beach and Fairview Beach and Somerset Beach. Near Ambar and Hampstead it runs along the edge of Caledon, and the first piece ends at Route 206 in Berthaville.
The second piece starts at US 301 near Owens, crosses Upper Machodoc Creek and runs down Tetotum Road to Tetotum.

moments.title: Passapatanzy
moments.text: In 1613 this was a Patawomeck village whose ruler, Japazaws, helped the English captain Samuel Argall take Pocahontas as a hostage.

moments.title: Fairview Beach
moments.text: Up Fairview Drive from the byway, a beach community of a few hundred people sits on the south bank of the Potomac.

moments.title: Caledon
moments.text: The road skirts an old-growth oak and tulip poplar forest on the plantation the Alexander brothers, founders of Alexandria, started in 1659, now a state park with bald eagle habitat along the Potomac.
